For statistical analysis, you can use Lee's L statistic for bivariate spatial correlation analysis, or another appropriate method of your choosing. You are testing whether NO2 in one place relates to Waste in NEIGHBORING places.

Determine whether the two variables show a significant bivariate spatial relationship. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement this directly using only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

# Build a dictionary of neighbors
neighbors = {b: [] for b in df_clean['borough']}
for _, row in adj_clean.iterrows():
    b = row['borough']
    n = row['neighbor']
    neighbors[b].append(n)

print('Neighbor counts:')

Thought: I need to build the adjacency matrix, compute Lee's L for bivariate spatial correlation, and run a permutation test with 1000 shuffles to assess significance.
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2022_no2_waste.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Clean data
df_clean = df.dropna().reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df_clean['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
print('n =', n)

# Build adjacency matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n))
borough_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b = row['borough']
    ne = row['neighbor']
    if b in borough_idx and ne in borough_idx:
        i = borough_idx[b]
        j = borough_idx[ne]
        W[i, j] = 1

# Symmetrize (ensure undirected) and zero diagonal
W = np.maximum(W, W.T)
np.fill_diagonal(W, 0)
S0 = W.sum()
print('S0 =', S0)

# Extract variables
x = df_clean['NO2_value'].values
y = df_clean['Waste_value'].values

# Standardize (mean-center)
zx = x - x.mean()
zy = y - y.mean()

# Lee's L statistic
numerator = zx.T @ (W @ zy)
denom = np.sqrt(zx @ zx) * np.sqrt(zy @ zy)
L_obs = (n / S0) * (numerator / denom)
print('Observed L =', L_obs)

# Permutation test: shuffle y values 1000 times
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 1000
L_perm = np.empty(n_perm)
for k in range(n_perm):
    y_perm = np.random.permutation(y)
    zy_perm = y_perm - y_perm.mean()
    num_perm = zx.T @ (W @ zy_perm)
    den_perm = np.sqrt(zx @ zx) * np.sqrt(zy_perm @ zy_perm)
    L_perm[k] = (n / S0) * (num_perm / den_perm)

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = np.mean(np.abs(L_perm) >= np.abs(L_obs))
print('Permutation p-value (two-tailed) =', p_value)
print('L_obs =', L_obs, 'p =', p_value)

# Also check one-tailed proportions for reference
prop_ge = np.mean(L_perm >= L_obs)
prop_le = np.mean(L_perm <= L_obs)
print('Proportion >= observed:', prop_ge)
print('Proportion <= observed:', prop_le)
```
